entities.evidence: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham, speaks to the king of Sodom.
Sodom names the city ruled by the king whom Abram addresses.
Yahweh is the divine name Abram invokes as he raises his hand in oath.
אֵל begins the title “God Most High,” which identifies Yahweh in Abram’s oath.
עֶלְיוֹן completes the title “God Most High,” repeating Melchizedek’s designation in Genesis 14:19.

analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָם אֶל מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, “Abram said to the king of Sodom,” אַבְרָם names the speaker.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:7 as an example of the existing sense to-a-person-speaking for אֶל.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל marks the person addressed.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:7, וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו introduces Yahweh’s words to Abram. The third-person suffix names the addressee from the narrator’s perspective, and Yahweh addresses him in the second person in הוֹצֵאתִיךָ.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָם אֶל מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, Abram is the speaker, and אֶל introduces the king of Sodom as the person he addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Link this occurrence to the existing sodom sense at word index 0 in the sedom place-name article.
draft.definition: סְדֹם names the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: In אֶל מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, “to the king of Sodom,” סְדֹם names the city ruled by the king whom Abram addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: יָדִי (“my hand”) is the direct object, and אֶל־יַהְוֶה (“toward Yahweh”) gives the direction of the gesture. Abram describes raising his hand to Yahweh in an oath.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, first person common singular. The ending ־תִי identifies Abram as the speaker and subject.
analysis.sense: raise or lift up a hand

draft.change: Add Gen.14.22 as an example of the existing Hebrew sense hand-limb.
draft.definition: The physical hand, here raised toward Yahweh in an oath.
draft.evidence: In Gen.14.22, הֲרִימֹתִי יָדִי identifies Abram’s hand as what he has raised.

analysis.evidence: Abram says הֲרִימֹתִי יָדִי אֶל יַהְוֶה, “I have raised my hand to Yahweh.” יָדִי is the direct object of “I have raised.” The suffix identifies the hand as Abram’s own, and אֶל יַהְוֶה gives the direction of the oath gesture.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew common noun, singular construct, with the first-person common singular possessive suffix ־ִי. The noun is tagged for both genders, and this verse has no agreement marker that narrows the reading.
analysis.sense: The physical hand raised in swearing an oath.

analysis.evidence: In הֲרִימֹתִי יָדִי אֶל יַהְוֶה, “I have raised my hand toward YHWH,” אֶל marks the direction of Abram’s oath gesture.
analysis.morphology: Simple Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: Abram raises his hand to יַהְוֶה and identifies him by the title אֵל עֶלְיוֹן, “God Most High.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, modified by עֶלְיוֹן.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69140:2, 69139:5, 69138:10.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective modifying אֵל, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Abram identifies יַהְוֶה as אֵל עֶלְיוֹן, God Most High. The title קֹנֵה governs שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ, “heaven and earth,” repeating Melchizedek’s designation of God in Genesis 14:19.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, used as a divine title.

analysis.evidence: In Abram’s oath, שָׁמַיִם and וָאָרֶץ together serve as the object of קֹנֵה. The pair “heavens and earth” encompasses all creation in the title Abram gives God Most High.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural, in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Abram calls God קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ. The pairing “heaven and earth” places earth opposite heaven and encompasses the whole world.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וָ means “and.” The noun אָרֶץ is the pausal form of אֶרֶץ, common gender, singular absolute.
